subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure on the span of an orthonormal n-frame is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure (reuse of the accepted declaration idtp_pc_plane_hausdorff_eq_map)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (Euclid P). Put ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i (s_i the coordinates of s ∈ ℝ^n = Euclid n), and Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}. Then the n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure H^n = μHE[n] restricted to Q is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure L^n (volume on ℝ^n) under ι: H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n), i.e. μHE[n].restrict Q = Measure.map ι volume. This is the comparator-accepted declaration idtp_pc_plane_hausdorff_eq_map, reused at its byte-identical frozen type.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) = Measure.map (fun s : Euclid n => ∑ i, s i • τ i) volume
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this child is the comparator-accepted declaration idtp_pc_plane_hausdorff_eq_map (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.integer_density_tangent_planes-a1.planar_constancy-a1.plane_measure_map-a1, status accepted, candidate ae1d8342b0e070140eb7cdd80292f9370a4dd8e5), taken at its byte-identical frozen type. The runtime keeps an accepted checkpoint as it is, so this reuse creates no node and no new proof work. Its accepted Lean proof was recompiled in this session against the frozen contract (b4d606db; Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, SimonGMT 2b36630); #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Use in this decomposition: with n = 2 and τ = ![a, e] it is steps 2–3 of the parent proof, H²⌞Q = ι_#(L²) for ι(s) = s₀a + s₁e. The reviewed proof follows.
Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; L^n := volume on ℝ^n = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); s_i are the coordinates of s ∈ ℝ^n; ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i; Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}. Nothing is assumed about n or P beyond τ being orthonormal (n = 0 is allowed: then Q = {0} and ι is the map from the one-point space ℝ^0 to 0).
1. (ι is a linear isometry.) ι is linear (ι(s + t) = ι(s) + ι(t), ι(cs) = cι(s)). For s ∈ ℝ^n, orthonormality gives ⟨ι(s), ι(s)⟩ = Σ_{i,k} s_i s_k ⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩ = Σ_i s_i² = ‖s‖² (Mathlib Orthonormal.inner_sum together with the Euclidean norm formula EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). Hence ‖ι(s)‖ = ‖s‖ for all s, and, ι being additive, ‖ι(s) − ι(t)‖ = ‖ι(s − t)‖ = ‖s − t‖: ι is an isometry (AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_of_norm).
2. (range ι = Q.) Each ι(s) = Σ_i s_i τ_i is a linear combination of τ_1, …, τ_n, hence lies in Q. Conversely, every y ∈ Q = span{τ_1, …, τ_n} can be written y = Σ_i c_i τ_i with c : Fin n → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun), i.e. y = ι(c) where c is regarded as the element of ℝ^n with coordinates c_i. So range ι = Q.
3. (Isometry invariance of μHE[n].) For an isometry f : X → Y between metric spaces carrying their Borel σ-algebras, the push-forward of μHE[d] under f is μHE[d] restricted to the range of f: (μHE[d]).map f = μHE[d].restrict (range f) (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; it expresses H^d(f(A)) = H^d(A), the isometry invariance of Hausdorff measure, together with the fact that f is a measurable embedding with image range f). Applying it to ι (step 1) with d = n and using step 2: (μHE[n] on ℝ^n).map ι = μHE[n].restrict (range ι) = μHE[n].restrict Q.
4. (Normalization.) On ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) the measure μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure: μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; the normalizing factor in the definition of μHE[n] is chosen exactly so that this holds).
5. (Conclusion.) Substituting 4 into 3: μHE[n].restrict Q = volume.map ι = Measure.map ι volume, i.e. H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n). ∎
proof_key_steps: ι(s) = Σ s_iτ_i is a linear isometry ℝ^n → ℝ^P by orthonormality (‖ι(s)‖² = Σ s_i²).
EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume: μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n, so H^n⌞Q = ι_#L^n.

subproblems.title: Lebesgue measure of the open square (−r, r)² and the closed square [−r, r]² in ℝ²
subproblems.statement: Let r ∈ ℝ with r ≥ 0, and let ℝ² = Euclid 2 = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) carry its volume (Lebesgue) measure, with coordinates v₀ = v 0 and v₁ = v 1. Then volume{v ∈ ℝ² : |v₀| < r and |v₁| < r} = 4r² and volume{v ∈ ℝ² : |v₀| ≤ r and |v₁| ≤ r} = 4r² (both as ENNReal.ofReal (4r²)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ r : ℝ, 0 ≤ r → volume {v : Euclid 2 | |v 0| < r ∧ |v 1| < r} = ENNReal.ofReal (4 * r ^ 2) ∧ volume {v : Euclid 2 | |v 0| ≤ r ∧ |v 1| ≤ r} = ENNReal.ofReal (4 * r ^ 2)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the parent-supplied proof (the boxes (−r, r)² and [−r, r]² have volume ofReal(2r)·ofReal(2r) = ofReal(4r²); PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, Real.volume_pi_Ioo, Real.volume_Icc_pi), isolated as a statement about Lebesgue measure on ℝ² alone.
Notation. ℝ² := Euclid 2 = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) with its volume (Lebesgue) measure; for v ∈ ℝ², v₀ := v 0 and v₁ := v 1 are its coordinates. φ := WithLp.ofLp : ℝ² → (Fin 2 → ℝ) is the map forgetting the L² structure, so (φ v) i = v i for i : Fin 2; Fin 2 → ℝ carries the product Lebesgue measure volume. Fix r ∈ ℝ with r ≥ 0.
1. (The coordinate map is measure preserving.) φ is measure preserving from volume on ℝ² to volume on Fin 2 → ℝ (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin 2)). Hence volume(φ⁻¹(B)) = volume(B) for every measurable B ⊆ Fin 2 → ℝ (MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage, a measurable set being null-measurable).
2. (The value 4r².) ∏_{i : Fin 2} ofReal(r − (−r)) = ofReal(2r)·ofReal(2r) (Fin.prod_univ_two) = ofReal(2r·2r) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, which needs 2r ≥ 0, true since r ≥ 0) = ofReal(4r²).
3. (Open square as a preimage.) For t ∈ ℝ, |t| < r ⟺ −r < t < r (abs_lt). The elements of Fin 2 are exactly 0 and 1, so |v₀| < r and |v₁| < r hold iff (φ v) i ∈ Ioo(−r, r) for every i : Fin 2. Thus {v : |v₀| < r ∧ |v₁| < r} = φ⁻¹(B°) with B° := Set.pi univ (fun _ : Fin 2 => Ioo(−r, r)).
4. (Open square.) B° is a product of open intervals, hence measurable (MeasurableSet.univ_pi with measurableSet_Ioo). By steps 1 and 3, volume{v : |v₀| < r ∧ |v₁| < r} = volume(B°) = ∏_{i : Fin 2} ofReal(r − (−r)) (Real.volume_pi_Ioo) = ofReal(4r²) (step 2).
5. (Closed square as a preimage.) For t ∈ ℝ, |t| ≤ r ⟺ −r ≤ t ≤ r (abs_le), and the order on Fin 2 → ℝ is pointwise. So {v : |v₀| ≤ r ∧ |v₁| ≤ r} = φ⁻¹(B̄) with B̄ := Icc (fun _ : Fin 2 => −r) (fun _ => r) ⊆ Fin 2 → ℝ.
6. (Closed square.) B̄ is a closed interval of Fin 2 → ℝ, hence measurable (measurableSet_Icc). By steps 1 and 5, volume{v : |v₀| ≤ r ∧ |v₁| ≤ r} = volume(B̄) = ∏_{i : Fin 2} ofReal(r − (−r)) (Real.volume_Icc_pi) = ofReal(4r²) (step 2). ∎
(No case split on r is needed: for r = 0 the open square is empty and the closed square is {0}, and both computations give ofReal 0 = 0.)
